sentences.text: The crux of the case of the prosecution could be summarised as follows;
The informant claims to be a resident of Beedi Colony, Gangavaram Mandalam, Palamaner, Chittor Taluk and is a lorry driver.
The informant claims to have four children, Mrs Yasmin, 25 years, Mrs.Syed Asma, 20 years, Syed Humera, 18 years and Syed Mainuddin, 16 years.
About 6 years prior to the unfortunate incident the informant claims that his daughter, Mrs Yasmin had  3 S.C.No. 35/2018 married Mr Syed Nayaz of Bangalore.
The couple were living happily at Palamaner for 5 years since their marriage.
The informant claims to have got a house constructed to the couple.

The couple have two children,
Miss Siddiqa of 4 years and miss ayesha of 2 years.

About 9 months prior to the incident the couple are said to have migrated to Bangalore and were residing in a rented house at no.117, 4 th cross, Nehru Colony,
Yarabnagar, Bangalore.
The accused was a carpenter by profession.
Thereafter the accused is alleged to have started demanding dowry to a tune of Rs.1 lakh.
However the informant claims to have told his daughter that it would not be possible for him to arrange for such a huge amount.

3. About 6 months prior to the incident the informant claims to have arranged for Rs.35,000-00 and Banashankari Ps vs Syed Nayaz on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44488474/
2 sent to the accused.
But the accused was ont satisfied  4 S.C.No. 35/2018 and had demanded the remaining amount.
In this regard the accused is alleged to have even meted out cruelty to the deceased both physical and mental.

On 5.11.2016 the deceased is said to have called up the informant and informed him of torture meted out by the accused to her asking her to get the remaining money from her parents' house in default she would be thrashed without mercy.
The informant had then consoled the deceased and told her that he was in delhi and once he is back he would arrange for the balance amount.
But unfortunately when the informant had returned he was informed by his relatives that his daughter had committed suicide by hanging on 8.11.2016 at about 10.00 a.m.
The informant was informed by the police that the body of his daughter was shifted to the kims hospital.
Hence the information was given to the police for investigation.
Accused is in Judicial custody.
Charge framed.
Accused has denied the charge against him and claimed to be tried.

To prove the case, the prosecution had examined five witnesses as PW.1 to 8, got marked 15 documents as Ex P.1 to 15 and material objects marked as M.O.1.

is opinion of the expert and Ex.P.15 (a) is the signature of the witness.

The witness had identified the photograph at Ex.P.2.

The witness was cross examined by the learned counsel for the accused but nothing appears to have Banashankari Ps vs Syed Nayaz on 4 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44488474/

In the absence of the witnesses in particular the related witnesses not supporting the case of the prosecution any amount of support from the investigating officer would not come to the aid of the prosecution.
The prime witnesses are found to have failed to whisper regarding the alleged cruelty meted out by the accused to the deceased.
Under such circumstances there is no other option left but to hold the points in the negative.
16. Point No.2:-

In view of my finding on point No.1 and the reasons discussed above, I proceed to pass the following:
 15   ORD ER
Acting under S.235(1) of Cr.P.C., the  accused is acquitted of the charge  brought against him.

The bail bonds of accused and that  of his surety shall continue for a period  of six months in terms of S.437(a) of  Cr.P.C., to ensure his appearance before  the higher court in case of appeal or  revision.
M.O.1 being worthless shall be  destroyed after the expiry of appeal  period.
